title: HashMap versus TreeMap
context: How do HashMap and TreeMap differ?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (2 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: HashMap stores entries in hash buckets. Get, put and remove are O(1) on average, with no order guarantee. TreeMap is a red-black tree sorted by key or by a comparator. Operations are O(log n), and it provides navigation methods such as firstKey, floorKey and subMap. Keys in a TreeMap must be comparable or the comparator must handle them, and a key whose compare result is inconsistent with equals causes subtle bugs. Use TreeMap when you need order or range queries.

points.title: Speed versus order
points.why: HashMap is faster on average. TreeMap keeps keys sorted and supports range queries.

points.title: Comparator consistency
points.why: TreeMap uses compareTo to decide key equality, so an inconsistent comparator loses entries.
